subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Gear Ratios: Speed vs. Torque
description: A micro-lesson that makes Gear Ratios: Speed vs. Torque usable.

hook.text: A 10-tooth gear driving a 40-tooth gear gives a 4:1 ratio. The output has four times the torque.

buildup.text: Gear ratio equals driven teeth divided by driving teeth. Higher ratio means more force, less speed.

discovery.text: Your car's first gear has a high ratio for climbing hills. Fifth gear has a low ratio for highway speed.

twist.text: A clock uses extreme ratios. The minute hand shaft turns 12 times for every one turn of the hour hand.

climax.text: Every machine that changes speed or force uses gear ratios — bikes, drills, wind turbines, mixers.

punchline.text: Gear ratio is the universal translator between speed and strength.

quiz.question: What does a higher gear ratio provide?
options: Higher output speed with lower torque
Higher output torque with lower speed
Equal increases in both speed and torque
